arxiv-2101-08608.title: Improving D-Optimality in Nonlinear Situations
arxiv-2101-08608.creator: Hana Sulieman
arxiv-2101-08608.description: Abstract Experimental designs based on the classical D-optimal criterion minimize the volume of the linear-approximation inference regions for the parameters using local sensitivity coefficients. For nonlinear models, these designs can be unreliable because the linearized inference regions do not always provide a true indication of the exact parameter inference regions.

arxiv-2110-13307.title: Institutional Incentives for the Evolution of Committed Cooperation: Ensuring Participation is as Important as Enhancing Compliance
arxiv-2110-13307.creator: The Anh Han
arxiv-2110-13307.description: Abstract 1 School of Computing, Engineering and Digital Technologies, Teesside University, Middlesbrough, UK TS1 3BA ⋆ Corresponding: The Anh Han (t.han@tees.ac.uk) Abstract Both conventional wisdom and empirical evidence suggest that arranging a prior commitment or agreement before an interaction takes place enhances the chance of reaching mutual cooperation.

arxiv-2112-05272.title: U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) local strings in generalized hybrid metric-Palatini gravity
arxiv-2112-05272.creator: Hilberto M. R. da Silva, Tiberiu Harko, Francisco S. N. Lobo, João Luís Rosa​​
arxiv-2112-05272.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hilberto M. R. da Silva, Tiberiu Harko, Francisco S. N. Lobo, João Luís Rosa​​. In this work we will explore U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) local cosmic string solutions in the context of the generalized hybrid metric-Palatini theory of gravity in its scalar-tensor representation. Using a general static cillindrically symmetric metric to find the dynamical equations for this particular case, we will simplify the equations by imposing boost invariance along t t and z z directions.

arxiv-2206-13370.title: Adaptive Decoding Mechanisms for UAV-enabled Double-Uplink Coordinated NOMA
arxiv-2206-13370.creator: Thanh Luan Nguyen, Georges Kaddoum, Tri Nhu Do, Daniel Benevides da Costa, and Zygmunt J. Haas
arxiv-2206-13370.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Thanh Luan Nguyen, Georges Kaddoum, Tri Nhu Do, Daniel Benevides da Costa, and Zygmunt J. Haas. In this paper, we propose a novel adaptive decoding mechanism (ADM) for the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled uplink (UL) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) communications. Specifically, considering a harsh UAV environment, where ground-to-ground links are regularly unavailable, the proposed ADM overcomes the challenging problem of conventional UL-NOMA systems whose performance is sensitive to the transmitter’s statistical channel state information and the receiver’s decoding order.

arxiv-2305-16469.title: Bayesian Reinforcement Learning for Automatic Voltage Control under Cyber-Induced Uncertainty
arxiv-2305-16469.creator: Abhijeet Sahu, and Katherine Davis
arxiv-2305-16469.description: Abstract Voltage control is crucial to large-scale power system reliable operation, as timely reactive power support can help prevent widespread outages. However, there is currently no built in mechanism for power systems to ensure that the voltage control objective to maintain reliable operation will survive or sustain the uncertainty caused under adversary presence.

arxiv-2311-10914.title: Multi-valent Ion Mediated Polyelectrolyte Association and Structure
arxiv-2311-10914.creator: Alec Glisman, Sriteja Mantha, Decai Yu, Eric Wasserman, Scott Backer, Zhen-Gang Wang
arxiv-2311-10914.description: Abstract Polyelectrolytes are commonly used to chelate multi-valent ions in aqueous solutions, playing a critical role in water softening and the prevention of mineralization. At sufficient ionic strength, ion-mediated polyelectrolyte–polyelectrolyte interactions can precipitate polyelectrolyte–ion complexes, a phenomenon known as “like-charge attraction”.

arxiv-2411-09586.title: Commodity Booms, Local State Capacity, and Development Thanks: We thank Lori Beaman, Michael Best, Jonas Hjort, Dean Karlan, Chris Moser, Gabriel Natividad, Suresh Naidu, Andrea Prat, Nancy Qian, Edoardo Teso, Chris Udry, Silvia Vannutelli, Ebonya Washington, and participants at the Columbia Develop
arxiv-2411-09586.creator: Dafne Murillo, Sebastian Sardon
arxiv-2411-09586.description: Abstract State capacity may shape whether natural resources generate prosperity, as it determines if windfalls are effectively turned into useful projects or wasted. We test this hypothesis studying the 2004-2011 mining boom in Peru, where mines’ profits are redistributed as windfall transfers to local governments.

arxiv-2411-12168.title: Sketch-guided Cage-based 3D Gaussian Splatting Deformation
arxiv-2411-12168.creator: Tianhao Xie, Noam Aigerman, Eugene Belilovsky, Tiberiu Popa
arxiv-2411-12168.description: Abstract 3D Gaussian Splatting (GS) is one of the most promising novel 3D representations that has received great interest in computer graphics and computer vision. While various systems have introduced editing capabilities for 3D GS, such as those guided by text prompts, fine-grained control over deformation remains an open challenge.

arxiv-2508-12408.title: Data-driven quantification and visualization of resilience metrics of power distribution system
arxiv-2508-12408.creator: Dingwei Wang, Salish Maharjan, Junyuan Zheng, Liming Liu, Zhaoyu Wang
arxiv-2508-12408.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dingwei Wang, Salish Maharjan, Junyuan Zheng, Liming Liu, Zhaoyu Wang. This paper presents a data-driven approach for quantifying the resilience of distribution power grids to extreme weather events using two key metrics: (a) the number of outages and (b) restoration time. The method leverages historical outage records maintained by power utilities and weather measurements collected by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to evaluate resilience across a utility’s service territory. The proposed framework consists of three stages.

pmc-10688004.title: Alterations of brain activity in patients with alcohol use disorder: a resting-state fMRI study
pmc-10688004.creator: Xia Ruan, Zhiyan Song, Jie Zhang, Tingting Yu, Jun Chen, Tiantian Zhou
pmc-10688004.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundAlcohol use disorder (AUD) has a negative impact on one’s health and wastes a lot of societal resources since it damages one’s brain tissue. Yet the knowledge of the neural mechanisms underlying alcohol addiction still remains limited. This study aims to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying alcohol addiction by using voxel-wise binarized degree centrality (DC), weighted DC and functional connectivity (FC) methods to analyze brain network activity in individuals with AUD.MethodsThirty-three AUD patients and 29 healthy controls (HC) participated in this study.

pmc-10738501.title: MEASURING DISTRESS IN DEMENTIA: A PILOT STUDY ON PERCEIVED MEMORY, DYADIC RELATIONSHIPS, AND SELF-EFFICACY
pmc-10738501.creator: Amanda MacNeil, Katherine Judge
pmc-10738501.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Prior literature has suggested that some individuals with dementia are capable of self-reporting details of their lived experience. With this, researchers have been increasingly interested in understanding what it is like to live with dementia from the individual’s perspective. To capture a more holistic image of the illness experience of individuals with dementia, it is important to consider how they perceive and cope with various aspects of their illness.

pmc-11343843.title: SignalingProfiler 2.0 a network-based approach to bridge multi-omics data to phenotypic hallmarks
pmc-11343843.creator: Veronica Venafra, Francesca Sacco, Livia Perfetto
pmc-11343843.description: Unraveling how cellular signaling is remodeled upon perturbation is crucial for understanding disease mechanisms and identifying potential drug targets. In this pursuit, computational tools generating mechanistic hypotheses from multi-omics data have invaluable potential. Here, we present a newly implemented version (2.0) of SignalingProfiler, a multi-step pipeline to draw mechanistic hypotheses on the signaling events impacting cellular phenotypes. pmc-12366180.title: The impact of health emergencies on nurses’ burnout: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12366180.creator: Yinxia Liang, Hongbin Peng, Xia Luo, Min Wang, Yun Zhang, Haimei Huang, Jiawen Zhu, Mei Chen, Weiyi Tian, Jinli Mo, Yuhong Nong, Yangfang Wang, Yingqiong Huang, Sumin Tan, Li Jiang, Wei Pan, Chuanyi Ning
pmc-12366180.description: BackgroundBurnout is a prevalent occupational phenomenon among healthcare workers. To evaluate the current evidence on nurses’ burnout and the impact of turnover intention during the pandemic is imperative.ObjectiveWe aimed to comprehensively synthesize and quantify the impact of health emergencies caused by the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak on nurses’ burnout and identify factors associated with the negative impact.

pmc-12498373.title: New insights into the stress response mechanisms of stress-resistant Listeria monocytogenes via multi-omics and cell morphological changes
pmc-12498373.creator: Hyunhee Hong, Eiseul Kim, Seung-Min Yang, Min-Cheol Lim, Hyun Jung Kim, Liping Yang, Hae-Yeong Kim, Si Hong Park
pmc-12498373.description: Listeria monocytogenes (Lm) can persist in stressful conditions such as low pH, temperature, and salt concentration. Omics approaches enable the investigation of biomolecular features at both the transcript and protein levels. This study aimed to understand stress response mechanisms by analyzing transcript and protein levels of stress-resistant L. monocytogenes (SR-Lm) under multiple stress conditions.

pmc-12690700.title: PDNO-14 SURVIVAL OUTCOMES OF PEDIATRIC LOW-GRADE GLIOMAS IN A MIDDLE-INCOME COUNTRY: EXPERIENCE FROM COTE D’IVOIRE
pmc-12690700.creator: Landry Drogba, Grâce Djonde, Marc Gbazi, Raissa Diaby, Joel Brou, Landry Konan
pmc-12690700.description: BackgroundPediatric low-grade gliomas, including glial and glioneuronal tumors, are the most common pediatric brain tumors. While outcomes are favorable in high-income countries, data from middle-income settings remain limited.ObjectiveTo evaluate survival outcomes and identify prognostic factors associated with tumor progression and mortality in children treated for Low-grade gliomas in Cote d’Ivoire.

pmc-12749705.title: Benchmarking proprietary and open-source language and vision-language models for gastroenterology clinical reasoning
pmc-12749705.creator: Seyed Amir Ahmad Safavi-Naini, Shuhaib Ali, Omer Shahab, Zahra Shahhoseini, Thomas Savage, Sara Rafiee, Jamil S. Samaan, Reem Al Shabeeb, Farah Ladak, Jamie O.
